parts.problem_md:
A circle has radius 8.5cm.

Work out the circumference of the circle. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
> *The formula for the circumference of a circle is*

$C=2πr$

> *Substitute the radius into the formula*

$C=2\timesπ\times8.5$

**[M1]**

$C=53.407...$

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures by checking whether the 4th digit of the number tells you to round up or not*

**Final answer:** **53.4**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **A1**: Answers in the range 53.3-53.43 will get this mark.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a shaded shape made from three identical semicircle, $X$,  $Y$ and $Z$

![Diagram with two semicircles on a line AE, touching at Y, marked B to D. Semicircles labelled X and Z. "Diagram NOT accurately drawn" noted.](assets/001-diagram-with-two-semicircles-on-a-line-ae-touchi.png)

$ABCDE$ is a straight line.

$AC$ is the diameter of semicircle  $X$and $B$ is the centre of semicircle   $X$ 
$BD$ is the diameter of semicircle $Y$ and $C$is the centre of semicircle  $Y$ 
$CE$ is the diameter of semicircle $Z$ and $D$ is the centre of semicircle $Z$

$AC=BD=CE=20\mathrm{cm}$

Work out the perimeter of the shaded shape. 
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
parts.solution_md:
> *The diameter of each circle is *$20\mathrm{cm}$

> *The circumference of each full circle would be*

$π\times20=62.83...$

**[M1]**

> *Divide by *$2$* to get the length of each curved part of the semicircle *

$62.83...\div2=31.41...$

> *There are three semicircles so find the total of the curved parts*

$31.41...\times3=94.24...$

> *Add on the two straight lines*

$94.24...+10+10=114.24...$

**[M1]**

> *Round to the nearest whole number*

$114$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Working is not required, so correct answer scores full marks.

parts.problem_md:
A wheel on a tractor has a diameter of 160 cm.

The tractor travels 1750 metres

Work out the number of complete turns made by the wheel. 
Show your working clearly
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert the metres to centimetres*

> **[exam-tip]**
> There are 100cm in 1m.

$1750\times100=175000$

**[M1]**

> *Work out the circumference of the wheel*

$π\times160=502.654...$

**[M1]**

> *Work out how many times the circumference would fit into the distance travelled*

$175000\div502.65=348.151...$

**[M1]**

> *Ignore the decimal places as the question asks for complete turns only*

**Final answer:** **348**

**[A1]**
